caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:002013
attempts.paper_title: Microinvasive Probes for Monitoring Electrical and Chemical Neural Activity in Nonhuman Primates

inputs.what: The paper's processed data on Zenodo; the four trial lists of session 09/26/2024 (large reward, small reward, left, right; successful trials) and the example beta power trace of the 35th large-reward trial, used by zenodo-link only. session126_events.mat was inspected for a code map of Monkey P's events and has none.

The paper's spike plotting code (spikes_PCA.m, ISI_Plot.m), read for the sorted unit (unit 1) and the 8 samples before threshold of the stored waveforms, used to align the spike-triggered average in the data check.

attempts.entry_title: Microinvasive probes for dopamine, LFP and spike recording in monkeys (Amjad et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: The paper's electrical findings held in this data, its dopamine findings only weakly or not at all, and its implant yield and longevity numbers could not be tested. LFP beta power was more suppressed after large-reward and contralateral cues, though reward and cue side change together across blocks, and a well-isolated sorted unit was found in monkey P. Dopamine was higher after large-reward cues, but weakly (p = 0.023), and the raw voltammetric current showed no dopamine redox signature. The yields and recording for over a year could not be tested without implant dates or sensor lists. The second dopamine channel is missing, and monkey P's event codes have no names, so its reward-related spiking could not be tested.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Amjad, Mahajan, Choi, Shrivastav, Murray, Somich, Coyne and Schwerdt (2025) on dandiset 002013, which holds the raw FSCV and trial-aligned dopamine of site c8dg (shape task), the raw EPhys and bipolar beta-band LFP of sites c3bs and c3a (direction task) of Monkey T, and the raw EPhys and sorted spikes of Monkey P. It checks the recording parameters, the task structure, the link to the paper's Zenodo deposit, the reward and side contrasts of dopamine and beta power, beta bursts, the raw FSCV voltammograms and the isolation of the sorted unit.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Amjad et al. (2025) from dandiset 002013
Earlier findings of amjad-2025-01 checked on version 0.261120.1306

outcomes.statement: Insertion yields were low, 21.4% (3 of 14 sensors) in monkey T and 33% (3 of 9) in monkey P, counted as recording sites that stayed functional after insertion until the end of the study.
outcomes.quote: insertion yields remained low ranging from 21.4% (3/14 individual sensors) in monkey T to 33% (3/9) in monkey P. These values indicate the number of recording sites that retained functionality after insertion, until the end of this study.
outcomes.notes: The criterion needs the list of implanted sensors per monkey and whether each kept recording. The files hold only the recorded sites (c8dg; c3bs and c3a; cl3, named ch33 in the units), and neither the files nor the dandiset metadata list the implanted sensors (14 in monkey T and 9 in monkey P by the paper). The asset metadata of the three files does not mention sensors (data check); the verifier found the same in its round-1 API check.

outcomes.statement: The s-µIPs kept recording for more than a year after implantation; the example sites were recorded 483 days (c8dg), 496 days (c3bs-c3a) and 390 days (monkey P) after implantation.
outcomes.source: Figure 3A, 3B and Figure 5 legends; Results and Discussion, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: sites c8dg and c8ds: 483 days postimplant ... site c3bs-c3a: 496 days postimplant ... site c33:390 days postimplant ... Measurements were made from chronically implanted s-μIPs that maintained functionality >1 year postimplant.
outcomes.notes: The criterion needs the implantation date of each site. No text field or attribute of the three files and nothing in the dandiset metadata gives one; the fields that mention implants are descriptions (notebook cell claim:chronic-duration). The subjects' ages (P11Y, P8Y), printed from the files and the asset metadata, are not implantation dates. The release notes of the pinned version say so too: "The implant dates are not given, so the days after implant that the paper reports cannot be checked".

outcomes.statement: FSCV applied a triangular waveform from -0.4 to 1.3 V at 400 V/s, every 100 ms (10 Hz).
outcomes.source: Methods, FSCV and EPhys Recordings, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: FSCV operates by applying a triangle waveform from −0.4 to 1.3 V at a rate of 400 V/s ... The triangular waveform is applied every 100 ms for an effective sampling frequency of 10 Hz.
outcomes.notes: Three of four values are within tolerance. Highest applied potential 1.3395 V, sweep rate 400.46 V/s (median step of the rising ramp times 24999.7 Hz), scan frequency 9.9999 Hz. The lowest stored potential is -0.3470 V, outside -0.4 +- 0.04 V, and the same across the session (-0.3479 to -0.3474 V over 11 blocks of 1000 scans). The dandiset description gives -0.35 to 1.34 V, as the stored voltage does. The holding potential between scans is not stored (the series has a gap between the 214-sample scans), so whether the electrode was held at -0.4 V between scans cannot be seen. Each stored scan starts at its lowest potential (sample 0, -0.347 V), peaks at sample 107 and ends at -0.3205 V.

outcomes.statement: EPhys was sampled at 30 kHz in monkey P and 32 kHz in monkey T, and band-pass filtered from 0.1 to 7500 Hz.
outcomes.source: Methods, FSCV and EPhys Recordings, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: EPhys recordings were made using a unity-gain analog amplifier headstage ... at a sampling frequency of 30 (monkey P) or 32 kHz (monkey T), and bandpass filtered from 0.1 to 7500 Hz.
outcomes.notes: Monkey P 29999.9997 Hz from the median timestamp interval of the first 2e6 samples; Monkey T 31999.9624 Hz from the rate of the 09/26/2024 raw series; the Neuralynx settings of both 09/26/2024 channels give DspLowCutFrequency 0.1 Hz and DspHighCutFrequency 8000 Hz. All four are within tolerance. The stored high cut is 8000 Hz where the paper and the dandiset description state 7500 Hz. Monkey P's electrodes table stores no filter settings, and the 09/13/2024 file holds no raw EPhys.

outcomes.statement: In the shape task, forced trials made up 25% of all trials, and the cue-reward association was reversed after blocks of 50 to 300 trials.
outcomes.quote: Forced choice trials were also interleaved (25% of all trials) where only one value cue was displayed ... The cue-reward association was reversed after a block of 50–300 trials depending on the session.
outcomes.notes: Forced trials (code 119) are 358 of 1468, 24.39%. In the 303 successful forced trials (142 with image 81, 161 with image 88, none with both) the large-reward image changes 9 times, giving 8 complete blocks of 71, 93, 121, 136, 153, 172, 194 and 273 trials (in session order 172, 153, 121, 71, 194, 93, 136, 273), all within 45 to 330; the first and last blocks, cut by the file, are 61 and 194 trials. Forced and choice trials (code 120) are disjoint and cover every trial.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset reproduces the processed data the paper deposited on Zenodo; the trial selections and the beta power of the paper's example trial computed from the dandiset agree with the paper's own files.
outcomes.quote: Data used in this study are available at zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14826579).
outcomes.notes: Trials matched by number. The Zenodo small and left lists agree with the selections decoded here for all 602 and 594 trials; the large and right lists for 569 of 570 and 577 of 578 (99.82% and 99.83%). The one trial only here is trial 1501, whose 60 s window ends at 24978.4 s, after the end of the LFP at 24965.4 s, which likely explains its absence from the paper's lists. The beta power computed here for the 35th large-reward trial (trial 84) correlates with the Zenodo trace at r = 0.9421 at lag 0 and 0.9427 at the best lag of 6 ms, median ratio 0.943. The dataset's measures match the paper's published values (the trace) and the dataset's own trial codes give the paper's lists, so the link holds on both sides. The example file's field trial35bigrewardata holds the time axis, not the LFP, so the raw example trace could not be compared. The four Zenodo lists are in ascending trial order without repeats, so their 35th entry is the 35th trial. The trace criterion was written after r = 0.94 was known, so that part is not an independent check. With the paper's order read literally (squared, then enveloped), r = 0.9132 at lag 0 and the median ratio is 1.689; the claims file's order matches the Zenodo trace more closely, though its range (14.1 to 2184.5e-12 V^2) is wider than Zenodo's (36.0 to 1559.6e-12).
deviations: The 35th trial of the large-reward list is read as the 35th entry of the Zenodo list (trial 84), as the file name and the claims file say; the list is in ascending order.

outcomes.statement: Dopamine was measured from two neighbouring channels of one dual-channel s-µIP (sites c8dg and c8ds, 0.1 to 0.2 mm apart), and both showed dopamine increases after the value cue in a single forced large-reward trial.
outcomes.quote: These measurements also demonstrate the ability to measure dopamine from two neighboring channels on a single s-μIP with 0.1–0.2 mm separation between the recording tips. ... (e.g., increases in both channels after the value cue, V).
outcomes.notes: The criterion needs the trial-aligned dopamine of both c8dg and c8ds. The 09/13/2024 file holds c8dg only, and the paper's Zenodo deposit holds only a c8dg file (FSCV_trlists_c8dg_09132024_firsthalf.mat). Not deciding, the c8dg half alone has a mean change above zero over 0 to 3 s in 65.9% of 85 forced large-reward trials with a value. The release notes of the pinned version list it as a known gap ("The second FSCV site of Figure 3A (c8ds) is not in the dandiset").

outcomes.statement: The single-trial FSCV colour plot shows dopamine redox current, with changes near 0.6 V (oxidation) and -0.2 V (reduction) after the value cue.
outcomes.quote: Color plot shows clear dopamine redox current (i.e., color changes ∼0.6 and −0.2 V).
outcomes.notes: In the mean background-subtracted voltammogram of the 164 successful forced large-reward trials, the most negative falling-sweep value (-0.048 nA) is at 0.897 V, outside -0.35 to -0.05 V, so the criterion fails. The largest rising-sweep value (0.074 nA) is at 0.512 V, inside 0.45 to 0.75 V, but the mean is flat within its noise and this is not an oxidation peak: at 0.608 V the mean change is -0.014 +- 0.020 nA and at -0.192 V -0.006 +- 0.018 nA (SEM), and with the cue moved by -10, -5, +5 and +10 s the rising maxima fall at 0.864, -0.240, 1.329 and -0.144 V. No redox signal is detectable: the single-trial change at 0.608 V has an SD of 0.259 nA over trials, so the mean would show about 0.04 nA or more. Over 2 to 3 s, where the table's da differs most, the change at 0.608 V is -0.045 +- 0.023 nA for large and -0.049 +- 0.025 nA for small reward (p = 0.938). With the 87 trials of the trial-aligned table neither extreme is in range (1.152 and 0.865 V); 8 of 164 single trials meet both ranges; with the cue moved one scan (0.1 s) either way the falling minimum is at -0.080 V and the rising maximum at 1.329 V, so one condition still fails. The raw current is on the trial clock (cross-correlation of the raw 0.6 V current with the table's iox, z 19.3 at lag -1 scan and 18.4 at lag 0). The stored PCA da shows a reward contrast (fig4a-dopamine-reward) where the raw current and the stored iox show none; the PCA weights are not in the dataset, so the source of that contrast cannot be checked. Figure 3A shows a single trial that cannot be identified in the files, so the mean over trials is the criterion's test, not the paper's display.
deviations: All 164 successful forced large-reward trials of the session are averaged, as the raw current covers the whole session; the 87 in the trial-aligned table are shown as a variant and give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Single-trial bipolar LFP from site c3bs-c3a shows beta bursts (one to a few cycles of high beta power) whose frequency changes around the cue and other task events.
outcomes.quote: Single-trial LFPs measured from another s-μIP are shown to display fluctuations in the frequency of β-band “bursts” (i.e., 1–few cycles of high β-band power) around the cue and other task events
outcomes.notes: With the 75th percentile threshold (356.2e-12 V^2) and bursts of at least 50 ms, the burst rate over 570 successful large-reward trials is 1.512 bursts/s in -1 to 0 s and 1.207 in 0 to 1 s from the value cue (240 trials fewer after, 123 more, 207 equal), Wilcoxon p = 9.5e-10. The variants also differ, at the 50th percentile 0.695 to 1.421 (p = 2.5e-47) and at the 90th 1.475 to 0.661 (p = 2.4e-45), so the rate changes at every threshold but its direction depends on the threshold. With the claims file's 0.25 s Hanning smoothing the runs above the 75th percentile last 206 ms at the median (10th to 90th percentile 70 to 583 ms) and 4.9% are shorter than 50 ms, so the minimum length removes almost nothing and these events are longer than the paper's bursts of one to a few cycles. Variants, not deciding; without the smoothing (median run 67 ms) the rate falls at the 75th percentile (3.074 to 2.105, p = 6.8e-34); with the paper's order read literally (squared, then enveloped) it falls at the 75th (1.318 to 1.077, p = 4.3e-07), rises at the 50th and falls at the 90th.
deviations: The threshold is the percentile over all trial windows, read as the union of the 60 s windows of the trials table; they cover every LFP sample, so it is the percentile of the whole series.

outcomes.statement: Trial-averaged dopamine at site c8dg is higher after large-reward than after small-reward value cues, in successful forced trials of the shape task.
outcomes.quote: Higher dopamine levels are observed following the display of large reward associated value cues as compared to small reward cues in monkey T
outcomes.notes: 168 successful forced trials have a row in the trial-aligned table (87 large, 81 small); 3 are dropped for a NaN at the value cue. Mean re-referenced da over 0 to 3 s, median 1.367 for large (n=85) and 0.191 for small (n=80), P(large > small) 0.603, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0226. Variants, not deciding; 1.5 to 3 s p = 0.00636, 0 to 1.5 s p = 0.334, da as stored p = 0.298, and the re-referenced iox shows no difference (large -0.015, small -0.001, p = 0.446). With the cue moved by -10, -5 and +5 s there is no difference (p 0.46 to 0.95); at +10 s small is higher (p = 0.00577). The table covers only trials 0 to 733 of 1468, as the paper's Zenodo file does. The window ends before feedback, which comes 3.75 to 4.03 s after the value cue in every successful forced trial. With the cue moved one scan either way p = 0.0272 (-0.1 s) and 0.0175 (+0.1 s). The evidence is weak; the p-value is near 0.05, three of four variants are not significant, the +10 s control also gives p < 0.05 (in the other direction), and the raw current shows no reward contrast at 0.6 V (fig3a-redox-peaks).
deviations: The window 0 to 3 s takes the 30 samples after the cue sample (samples +1 to +30), a standard choice; the cue sample is the nearest 10 Hz sample, as the claims file says.

outcomes.statement: Beta-band LFP power at c3bs-c3a in the direction task is more suppressed (stronger event-related desynchronization) after large-reward than after small-reward value cues, in a brief window after the cue.
outcomes.quote: Trial-averaged β-band LFP power for large and small reward conditions in the direction task, showing increased suppression (i.e., ERD, highlighted in yellow) for large as compared to small reward cues during the brief time window following the value cue at 0 s
outcomes.notes: Mean beta power over 0 to 0.5 s after the value cue, median 275.1e-12 V^2 for large reward (n=570) against 327.2e-12 for small (n=602), P(large < small) 0.597, p = 1.03e-08; divided by the -0.5 to 0 s baseline 0.455 against 0.553 (p = 1.09e-06). The difference is confined to the brief window; over 0 to 1 s (p = 0.09, large median higher) and 0.25 to 0.75 s (p = 0.658) it is not significant, with or without the baseline. The side of the big reward is fixed within 16 blocks of 50 to 93 successful trials ("The big and small reward locations were changed on every block", Methods, Behavioral Tasks), so large against small is also one side against the other within a block. With the side fixed the difference holds (left cues 244.5 against 290.3, p = 0.00164; right cues 301.9 against 394.2, p = 9.91e-08), and the large median is below the small one in 12 of 16 blocks (Wilcoxon over blocks p = 0.025). Within a block large against small is the same contrast as left against right, so the blocks cannot separate a reward effect from a side effect; the 12 are all 8 blocks with the big reward on the left, where both effects predict the same sign, and 4 of the 8 with the big reward on the right (5, 7, 11 and 13), where they predict opposite signs. This fits two additive effects and equally a single effect confined to the left-big blocks. The side-fixed tests compare trials from different blocks. The criterion as written is met. With the paper's order read literally (squared, then enveloped) 378.8 against 409.0, p = 5.42e-06.

outcomes.statement: With the reward fixed at large, beta-band LFP power is more suppressed when the cue is on the left (contralateral) than on the right (ipsilateral).
outcomes.quote: Increased suppression for contralateral is observed as compared to ipsilateral movement conditions.
outcomes.notes: In successful large-reward trials, mean beta power over 0 to 0.5 s, median 244.5e-12 V^2 for left cues (n=282) against 301.9e-12 for right (n=288), P(left < right) 0.616, p = 1.61e-06; with the baseline 0.389 against 0.546 (p = 2.07e-09). Over 0 to 1 s left is also lower (p = 0.0188; 0.000136 with the baseline), over 0.25 to 0.75 s not (p = 0.75 and 0.0751). Small-reward trials show the same side difference (290.3 against 394.2, p = 1.48e-10). Large-reward left and right trials come from different blocks of the side-reward mapping. Taking each block's median as one value, the 8 left blocks are lower than the 8 right blocks (251.0 against 306.8, p = 0.000622); within blocks over both rewards left is below right in 12 of 16 (Wilcoxon p = 0.00336), all 8 left-big blocks and 4 of 8 right-big blocks (1, 3, 9 and 15). Within a block left against right is the same contrast as large against small, so the blocks cannot separate a side effect from a reward effect; the main test holds the reward fixed but compares different blocks. With the paper's order read literally (squared, then enveloped) 363.2 against 393.4, p = 0.00734.

outcomes.statement: Spikes recorded from an s-µIP in the caudate of monkey P (site c33, 390 days post implant) fire at a different rate for large and small reward during the value cue fixation of the direction task.
outcomes.quote: Spike measurements from an s-μIP in the CN of monkey P also displayed reward-modulated differences in firing rate during the value cue fixation window
outcomes.notes: The criterion needs the value cue time and reward size of each trial. Monkey P's file has no trials table, and its 36 event codes are stored as 'TTL code N' with the description 'The code map for this session is not available'. The paper's Zenodo deposit holds the same 20812 events (session126_events.mat, inspected while preparing, not in the notebook) as Neuralynx TTL strings without names, and the paper's code (doi:10.5281/zenodo.10397773, spikes_PCA.m, ISI_Plot.m, percent_recovery.mlx) does not name them. The direction-task code map of the 2024 sessions cannot be carried over, as the 2018 codes differ (for example no code 128 and no code 101). The release notes of the pinned version say "Monkey P's 36 event codes have no names, so its trials and reward conditions cannot be identified", and that the codes are stored by code "since no code map exists for that session".

outcomes.statement: The s-µIP recorded a spike-sorted unit in monkey P, shown by its average waveform and its interspike interval histogram.
outcomes.quote: Average spike waveform ± standard deviation. ... Interspike interval (ISI) histogram showing the distribution of the timing between spikes detected.
outcomes.notes: Unit ch33#1 (Plexon unit 1, identical to thresholded unit 1) has 1 interspike interval under 1 ms of 31246 (0.0032%). Its mean stored waveform has a trough of 30.6 uV, 4.58 times the noise of 6.69 uV (MAD/0.6745 of the 300 to 6000 Hz signal) over the first 600 s of the recording, and 5.62 and 5.50 times in two later 600 s segments. The unsorted cluster ch33#0 has 11.633% of its intervals under 1 ms. In the first segment 10.7% of raw samples sit at the +-1 mV input limit. Leaving out samples within 1 ms of the input limit the ratio is 4.48, 5.90 and 5.78; the trough of the spike-triggered average of the same 300 to 6000 Hz signal is 34.9 to 35.5 uV, 5.21 to 6.50 times the noise.
deviations: The 600 s of the noise estimate are the first 600 s of the recording, a standard choice; two later segments are shown and give the same outcome. The band-pass is a 4th-order Butterworth run forwards and backwards, a standard choice.

findings.statement: The second channel of the dual-channel probe (site c8ds), whose dopamine the paper shows with c8dg in Figure 3A, is not in the dataset; the 09/13/2024 file holds c8dg only.

Monkey P's session (08/13/2018) has no trials table and its event codes have no names ('The code map for this session is not available'), so the value cue, the reward size and the trials of the direction task cannot be identified, and the reward-related spiking of Figure 5A cannot be tested.
No implantation dates and no list of implanted sensors are given in the files or the dandiset metadata, so the days post-implant and the insertion yields the paper reports cannot be checked.
The Neuralynx settings stored for both 09/26/2024 channels give a high cut of 8000 Hz, while the dandiset description (and the paper) state a band-pass of 0.1 to 7500 Hz.

The stored FSCV applied voltage runs from -0.347 to 1.340 V, as the dandiset description says (-0.35 to 1.34 V), where the paper states -0.4 to 1.3 V. The holding potential between scans is not stored.
Monkey P's recording site is named cl3 in the electrodes table and the descriptions, while the sorted units are named ch33#0 and ch33#1 and the paper names the site c33.

The trial-aligned FSCV series (da, iox, ph, m) are stored with 'Units unknown', and the table covers only trials 0 to 733 of the 1468 trials of 09/13/2024 without saying so. The regression slope of the iox change on the raw current change in nA is about 0.001.

The raw FSCV current of c8dg, which is on the trial clock, shows no dopamine redox signature after large-reward value cues on average (falling-sweep minimum at 0.897 V, change at 0.6 V of -0.014 +- 0.020 nA), and the stored iox shows no reward difference, while the stored PCA dopamine of the same trials does (p = 0.0226). The data do not show whether this is an error or a small signal.
findings.checked: Finding 8 is the raw FSCV current against the PCA da. minor is acceptable there, because the files do not show which of the two is wrong (cells 43, 49).

findings.statement: Monkey P's raw signal reaches the +-1 mV limit of the input range in 2.9 to 10.7% of samples in the three 600 s segments checked.

The events, the trials tables, the bipolar LFP, the raw EPhys and the raw FSCV current agree on one clock (raw against LFP at lag 0 to 1 ms, raw FSCV against the trial-aligned table within 0.1 s), Monkey P's spikes lie on its raw signal within 0.1 ms, the events are stored once each, and the trial selections of 09/26/2024 match the paper's Zenodo lists except the last trial.
findings.checked: None of the 11 findings is rated critical, and none should be. The clock checks support the "none" finding (cells 7, 13, 17, 21, 22).

findings.statement: The trials tables of both Monkey T sessions hold only 60 s windows around each trial start and one tag, with no trial conditions, so the conditions must be decoded from the event codes. Session 09/13/2024 has no small-reward code (100), and codes 35 and 36 are labelled 'right cue reward condition 1' and '2' without saying that they mark large and small reward, which they do in all 303 successful forced trials (164 and 139).

reconciliation.blind_note: The author saw no record, entry, notebook or transcript of amjad-2025-01, but it saw summaries of that attempt's results through two texts left in its checkout. The claims file's opening comment, written by the earlier author after its data check, says that the events repeat about five times, that the raw 09/26/2024 ephys and Monkey P's spikes are offset from the trial clock, and that the raw FSCV could not be matched to the trial-aligned traces and shows no reward contrast (earlier findings 1, 6, 8 and 9); the author's report says it read this before its own analysis (transcripts/amjad-2025/author-report.md, "Earlier results"). The release notes of 0.261120.1306, printed in its data check, list the problems "found by a reproduction attempt" and their fixes (earlier findings 1 and 5 to 10, and part of 13) and the known gaps. The three lines printed by tools/blind.sh audit are a link to the pilot notes and the run's own URL.

outcomes.note: On 0.261012.0921 the raw FSCV scan times were a 0.1 s grid from the first trial start and the raw current matched the stored iox at no offset (|r| below 0.06), so the earlier attempt blocked the claim as metadata_insufficient; 0.261120.1306 places each scan on the session clock (release notes, "Raw FSCV"), and the later attempt found it on the trial clock (cross-correlation z 19.3 at lag -1 scan) and tested the criterion. Its voltammogram of 164 trials has its falling-sweep minimum at 0.897 V, outside -0.35 to -0.05 V, and is flat within noise, as the earlier voltammogram at the old times also was (not deciding there).

entries.title: Microinvasive probes for dopamine, LFP and spike recording in monkeys (Amjad et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Amjad, Mahajan, Choi, Shrivastav, Murray, Somich, Coyne and Schwerdt (2025) on dandiset 002013, which holds the raw FSCV and trial-aligned dopamine of site c8dg (shape task), the raw EPhys and bipolar beta-band LFP of sites c3bs and c3a (direction task) of Monkey T, and the raw EPhys and sorted spikes of Monkey P. It checks the recording parameters, the task structure, the link to the paper's Zenodo deposit, the reward and side contrasts of dopamine and beta power, beta bursts, the raw FSCV voltammograms and the isolation of the sorted unit.
